name: Template: global catastrophic risks (AI, pandemics, nuclear war)
summary: TEMPLATE: what the charity does against which risks (AI, pandemics, nuclear war), the year, which branches carry the result (field work, a policy win, people trained), the year modelled, the bottom line in years of healthy life per $1,000 (quote it live in the write-up), and the biggest uncertainty. Say that the result rests on shared forecasts and a typical project's effect, so it moves with the AI slider and the discount rate.

source.title: charityevals' estimate: global catastrophic risks (AI, pandemics, nuclear war)

sections.title: Cost
sections.explainer: What the modelled program cost in the year the outcomes below are counted for, including its share of overhead. From audited financial statements or the annual report.

sections.title: Reach
sections.explainer: How many people, animals or meals the spending reached in the same year, as the charity reports it.

sections.title: Effect per unit
sections.explainer: What the intervention does for each unit reached, from the best available studies, before any adjustment.

sections.title: Adjustments
sections.explainer: Discounts for weaker evidence, what would have happened anyway, credit shared with others, and delivery falling short. All multiply the outcome.

sections.title: Other outcomes, in this model's unit
sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for outcomes in more than one unit (docs/normalization.md 2.6): each outcome is counted in its own unit (units of value for income and deaths, WELLBYs for life satisfaction, tonnes of CO₂e, chicken pain days) and put into this model's unit by its unit's conversion over this unit's, which the headline's conversion cancels. So each moves only with its own sliders, exactly as in a model of its own unit. The rows are fixed; don't edit them.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.explainer: The outcome in the family's shared unit, per dollar.

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: Staff who earn less than they could elsewhere pay part of the cost in kind. With credit by share of resources, your dollar is credited with its share of the full cost only.

Other currencies: a row in local currency times @fx.usd_per_<cur>_<year> (the IRS yearly average, else the World Bank's; add the fact with scripts/link-fx.py), never a typed rate.

rows.explainer: Spreads management and fundraising over programs in proportion to their cost, as GiveWell and ACE do.

Years the shared forecasts cover
rows.explainer: From the year the chances were forecast to 2100: turns a chance by 2100 into a yearly one. Fixed.

rows.label: Deaths in a catastrophe that ends humanity's future
rows.explainer: Everyone alive. Fixed.

rows.label: Share of the deaths that are of children under five
rows.explainer: A global catastrophe kills every age alike: the world's age split (@death_ages.population_world_*). Fixed.

Of the deaths at 15 or older, share aged 15 to 49
Value of a death averted (units of value)
rows.explainer: GiveWell's moral weights by age band × your value of a life, the site's one value of a death; no premium for a catastrophe's size.

rows.label: Discounted future years of healthy life per person of the long-run population, if the future ends now
rows.explainer: The site's one count of future generations (docs/normalization.md 2.19): the healthy years of people not yet born, discounted for ever at the shared rate. People alive now die in the catastrophe and are counted as deaths, so this stream rises from nothing to the long-run population over one lifetime (@catastrophe.life_expectancy_now) and then runs on: about 8 years at the default 4%, about 960 at the 0.1% floor. Fixed; don't edit.

rows.label: Future healthy years lost if humanity's future ends
rows.explainer: The long-run world population's healthy years, of people not yet born, discounted at the shared rate: your discount rate is how much future generations count.

rows.label: Years a cut in the risk counts before it would have come anyway
rows.explainer: The site's one answer (docs/normalization.md 2.9): work, a won policy or a trained person's career brings a cut in the risk forward by these years; Rethink Priorities' 15-25 years of persistence is replaced by it.

rows.label: AI: yearly chance of a catastrophe that ends humanity's future
rows.explainer: The shared chance by 2100 spread over the forecasts' years (@catastrophe, from the Existential Risk Persuasion Tournament, the AI chance your slider). Fixed; don't edit.

rows.explainer: The tournament's catastrophes (over 10% of the people alive die within five years) less the extinction-level ones, per year. Fixed; don't edit.

rows.label: AI: yearly chance of a smaller catastrophe
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: a smaller ai disaster the work also lowers (a single nuclear detonation in a city, a limited war; an AI incident that kills thousands), per year, from a published forecast or record, and its deaths in the next row; 0 with this reason where none is sourced. A shared figure another model could reuse goes into facts/catastrophe.json and is read here. Unused by default, so no source: when the model uses it, relabel it observed or estimate and cite the document.

rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: the deaths in the smaller disaster above, from the same source; 0 when the row above is 0. Unused by default, so no source: when the model uses it, relabel it observed or estimate and cite the document.

rows.label: AI: deaths in a catastrophe the world survives
rows.explainer: Everyone alive × the shared share such a catastrophe kills (over the tournament's 10% threshold; @catastrophe.<area>_catastrophe_death_share). Fixed.

rows.label: AI: share of the AI spending on work against misuse (dangerous-capability evaluations, defences against misuse)
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: of the AI spending, the share aimed at misuse, people using AI to do harm: bio, cyber and chemical uplift evaluations, unlearning hazardous knowledge, refusal and robustness (jailbreak) work aimed at misuse. The rest is misalignment work (alignment, interpretability, control, governance of loss of control); work aimed at both counts there. It weights Rethink Priorities' misuse preset (@catastrophe.ai_misuse_extinction_cut_per_million, ai_misuse_catastrophe_cut_per_million) against its misalignment one (@catastrophe.ai_extinction_cut_per_million, ai_catastrophe_cut_per_million) in the two rows per $1 million. From the charity's named outputs and their spending; 0 with the reason where none of its AI work is aimed at misuse; the high end for outputs that could be read either way.

rows.label: AI: expected deaths a year from these catastrophes
rows.formula: ai_extinction_per_year * deaths_if_extinct + ai_catastrophe_per_year * ai_deaths_if_catastrophe + ai_smaller_per_year * ai_smaller_deaths
rows.explainer: Each size's yearly chance × the people it kills.

rows.label: AI: expected future healthy years lost a year (extinction-level)
rows.explainer: Only a catastrophe that ends humanity's future takes the future; the world recovers from the others.

rows.label: AI: deaths averted a year by a typical $1 million of work, while its cut counts
rows.formula: ((1 - ai_misuse_cost_share) * @catastrophe.ai_extinction_cut_per_million + ai_misuse_cost_share * @catastrophe.ai_misuse_extinction_cut_per_million) * ai_extinction_per_year * deaths_if_extinct + ((1 - ai_misuse_cost_share) * @catastrophe.ai_catastrophe_cut_per_million + ai_misuse_cost_share * @catastrophe.ai_misuse_catastrophe_cut_per_million) * (ai_catastrophe_per_year * ai_deaths_if_catastrophe + ai_smaller_per_year * ai_smaller_deaths)
rows.explainer: The share of each yearly risk a typical $1 million of work in the area removes (Rethink Priorities' cross-cause model, its backfire step included; shared), × the deaths that risk carries: misuse work at Rethink's misuse preset, other AI work at its misalignment preset, weighted by ai_misuse_cost_share. The catastrophe figure also applies to the smaller size. Fixed; don't edit.

rows.label: AI: future healthy years kept a year by a typical $1 million of work
rows.explainer: As ai_deaths_per_million, for the future lost in an extinction-level catastrophe: the two presets' extinction cuts weighted by ai_misuse_cost_share.

rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: the spending behind the specific win below (a treaty, law, regulation, standard or institution launched), left out of the areas' shares; 0 with the reason without such a win in the year. Several wins: a pol2_ branch each. Feeds only the check cost_shares_total.

rows.label: Policy win: wins of this kind in the year
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: treaties, laws, regulations, standards or institutions won or launched in the year that the policy branch values (one kind per branch; a pol2_ branch for another); 0, with the reason, without one: then the branch counts nothing.

rows.label: Policy win: chance it happens because of this work
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: for a pending bill, treaty or standard, the chance of winning from a reference class (similar measures passed or failed); for a win already in the year, 1 (then delete single_event) and the charity's part of it in pol_counterfactual_adj and pol_attribution_share. Name the reference class.

rows.label: Policy win: share of the area's yearly risk it removes while in force
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: how much of the area's catastrophe risk the measure removes once in force: the share of the risk's pathways it touches × how well it closes them, anchored on published estimates of the mechanism (screening coverage, verification, a hotline's use). Calibrate it per risk, since a typical dollar's cut differs by orders of magnitude between areas (the default 1% fits nuclear policy, about $30 million of typical nuclear work, but is tens of billions of dollars of typical AI misalignment work): everyone's resources behind the measure (all its drafters and campaigners, not only the charity) × the area's cut per $1 million (@catastrophe.<area>_catastrophe_cut_per_million, and the extinction one for the future) is a typical project's cut, then a named multiple of it for how much more directly the measure acts. Check both sizes: pol_relative_cut ÷ each cut per $1 million is the millions of typical work it equals, to set against those resources and the field's yearly spending. Name the anchors.

Deaths averted that are in a COVID-scale pandemic (a part of deaths_averted)
rows.explainer: A natural or zoonotic pandemic on COVID's scale kills mostly older people, so its deaths are valued at COVID-19's age mix; every other size (a catastrophe that kills a share of the world, extinction) at the world's.
